record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
record.original_question: Determine for which hypersurfaces M of Sⁿ⁺¹ the following holds: M is a Dupin hypersurface, meaning that the multiplicities of its principal curvatures are constant and each principal curvature is constant along its principal directions; M is of finite type in the sense that its position vector field has a finite spectral decomposition into Laplace eigenmaps; and M is isoparametric, meaning that it has constant principal curvatures. Specifically, when is a Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere of finite type, and when is a finite-type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere isoparametric?

evidence.quote: The immersion x is said to be of finite type if the position vector field of M in E^m... can be expressed as a finite sum of E^m-valued eigenfunctions of the Laplace operator.
a hypersurface of an (n + 1)-sphere is called isoparametric if it has constant principal curvatures.
A hypersurface M of S^(n+1) is called a Dupin hypersurface if the multiplicities of the principal curvatures are constant and each principal curvature are constant along its principal directions.
Problem 4. When is a Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere to be of finite type? When is a finite type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere to be isoparametric?
As far as the author know, no further results were known for this problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{n+1} \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ denote the unit hypersphere in Euclidean $(n+2)$-space. An isometric immersion $x : M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ of a Riemannian manifold $M$ is said to be of finite type if the position vector field $x$ admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$x = x_0 + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $x_0$ is a constant vector in $\mathbb{E}^m$ and each $x_i$ ($1 \le i \le k$) is a non-constant $\mathbb{E}^m$-valued map on $M$ satisfying $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for some real number $\lambda_i$, with $\Delta$ the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced metric on $M$.

A hypersurface $M$ of $S^{n+1}$ is called Dupin if the multiplicities of its principal curvatures are constant on $M$ and each principal curvature is constant along the integral leaves of its associated principal distribution. A hypersurface $M$ of $S^{n+1}$ is called isoparametric if all of its principal curvatures are constant functions on $M$.

Solve the following two questions:

(a) Characterize all Dupin hypersurfaces of $S^{n+1}$ that are of finite type (when the inclusion $M \hookrightarrow S^{n+1} \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ is regarded as a Euclidean immersion).

(b) Determine whether every Dupin hypersurface of $S^{n+1}$ that is of finite type must be isoparametric, and if not, classify the exceptions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Research on Dupin hypersurfaces of finite type and their relation to isoparametric hypersurfaces continues, with partial results obtained under additional hypotheses (e.g., constant mean/scalar curvature, low number of distinct principal curvatures, Chern-conjecture-style assumptions), but a full classification of finite-type Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres and a complete answer to whether finite type forces isoparametricity has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Chern's Conjecture in the Dupin case
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work showing closed proper Dupin hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature are isoparametric under additional assumptions on the number of principal curvatures.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on conditions forcing Dupin hypersurfaces to be isoparametric, indicating the general question is not yet resolved.

status_evidence.title: Constructions of Compact Dupin Hypersurfaces with Non-constant Lie Curvatures
status_evidence.snippet: New constructions of compact proper Dupin hypersurfaces with non-constant Lie curvatures, showing the Dupin class is strictly larger than the isoparametric class.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates ongoing research into non-isoparametric Dupin hypersurfaces, supporting that the finite-type/isoparametric question remains active.

status_evidence.title: Isoparametric and Dupin Hypersurfaces (SIGMA survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on isoparametric and Dupin hypersurfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Survey discusses open problems relating Dupin and isoparametric conditions.
